description:
Erection of a purpose‑built, free‑standing wooden bike shed with living (green) roof in front porch area

Design & Purpose
A bespoke, sustainably‑constructed timber bike shed designed to fit our porch layout, providing secure and weatherproof storage for at least five bicycles (adult and child sizes). Intended to meet London planning requirements for cycle parking—secure, integrated, convenient, and accessible—aligned with London Cycle Design Standards and Policy T5 Cycling within the London Plan 2021.

Sustainability & Green Features
The shed is entirely constructed from sustainably sourced timber (e.g. Scottish larch) and topped with a living (“green”) roof. This roof supports biodiversity, softens visual impact, reduces stormwater runoff, and contributes to local pollution mitigation and the urban heat island effect—consistent with ecological guidelines. By contributing to biodiversity net‑gain and environmental stewardship, it is intended to be consistent with national policy encouraging vegetation on built structures.

Secure Storage for Active Travel
As a family of two adults and three children, we are committed to promoting active, green travel. There is very limited outdoor space for bike storage, and bike theft is a regular issue on our street. This shed will ensure accessible, convenient, and secure cycle parking, supporting the London-wide strategy to encourage cycling as a healthier, low‑carbon transport option.

Safety & Community Considerations
Following police advice, a large bush previously situated in this space—used for concealment during anti-social behaviour—has been removed. This shed, occupying a similar footprint, enhances safety by replacing informal foliage with a robust, secure structure whilst maintaining a tidy appearance and good visibility into our front porch from the main road consistent with police recommendations.

Planning & Compliance
The shed and this proposal accord with the objectives of the National Planning Policy Framework, the London Plan (particularly Policies T5, G1, G5), and the LBHF Local Plan (Policies OS5, T3, CC1 and CC2) by promoting sustainable transport, reducing reliance on private cars, contributing to urban greening and biodiversity through the living roof, and using natural materials that respect the character of the area. The structure is single‑storey, well proportioned to the space, and crafted to be visually appropriate to our streetscape—distinct from bulky or intrusive garage‑style sheds which may not comply.
